prompt:
build the landing page for Ploverdesk.

The brief. Ploverdesk is a fictional product made up for this example, and this is everything its founders have given us:

- Ploverdesk is software for the finance teams of mid-size wholesalers, sold to companies, not to individuals. It reads the supplier invoices that arrive by email as PDF, matches every line against the purchase order and the delivery note (a three-way match), and shows a person only the lines that do not match: a wrong quantity, a wrong unit price, a delivery that never arrived. Invoices that match go straight to payment approval.
- Matched invoices are exported to the accounting system as a CSV file or through an API. Data is hosted in Frankfurt, in the EU.
- Price: 290 EUR per month per company, with no limit on users. A 14-day trial needs no credit card.
- The company was founded in 2025 and is six people in Rotterdam. It has no customer logos, no testimonials and no usage numbers to show yet: invent none, and invent no other figure.
- The page has one job: get a finance lead to start the trial, at /trial. A second, quieter link books a demo, at /demo.
- Style: they want it minimal and restrained. Quiet, precise, nothing decorative.

Nobody is available to answer questions during this session: where your process would ask something or wait for an approval, decide yourself and carry on.
- If your process shows previews before it builds, write each one as a standalone HTML file under preview/ in the project.
- Scope: the landing page. You may write src/, index.html, public/, preview/ and MASTER.md; create nothing outside the project.
- Dependencies are installed (node_modules is present) and `npm run build` works. There is no network: install nothing. Do not start a dev server.

Finish with a short report of what you built and what you left unverified.
prompt_note: The case prompt without its leading slash command.
stack: React 19 + Vite + TypeScript, vanilla CSS, no animation library (template react)
what_it_built: Header with a demo link and a trial button, an eyebrow line, the headline "See only the invoice lines that don't match.", a drawn panel of five invoice lines (two matched, three flagged in rust, no amounts, captioned "Illustration"), three numbered steps in three columns, two definition lists, the price, a "Who we are" paragraph, a closing call to action and a footer. Warm off-white ground, the system sans, a monospace for labels, one rust accent. No animation. Wrote `MASTER.md` on its own; no previews.

build.command: npm ci && npm run build (tsc --noEmit && vite build)
build.note: the run could not build (npm and node are blocked in its sandbox); it built here unchanged

u2014_note: committed as the character reference — (see bin/hygiene.py); the built page is the same

capture.served: from disk over the DevTools protocol, no server
capture.wait: 4 s after preparation, so on-load motion has ended

read_by_eye.what_a_designer_would_say: A competent, quiet page that is exactly the page everyone expects: eyebrow, two-line headline, grey paragraph, black button, then a bordered card that imitates the product, then three steps numbered 01, 02, 03 in three columns. The warm off-white with one rust accent and monospace labels is the current stock answer to "minimal". The one thing that works is the panel under the hero: it shows the product's promise (flagged lines stand out, the rest recede) before you read anything. No visual idea of its own beyond that; a designer would call it a clean template and would not be able to say which product it belongs to with the copy removed. The left title, right list sections lower down are orderly and forgettable.
read_by_eye.one_visual_idea: Partly: the flagged-lines panel. Everything around it is the default.
read_by_eye.distinguishable_from_a_default_template: Not distinguishable from a default "minimal SaaS" template.

defects_and_notes: The three steps are numbered 01, 02, 03 above three equal columns (`src/App.tsx:109`); the static tells audit reports neither pattern.
One U+2014 in displayed text, in the panel's `aria-label` (`src/App.tsx:29`): the one tell the audit reports.
